properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha1@0.6.1 is declared in the workspace Cargo.lock — the SHA-1 digest ships in the build (transitive provider; no first-party call site found in the application code, which uses blake2/keccak/sha2/sha3). Presence is what the dependency inventory records; SHA-1 is collision-broken so any emergent use would be a weak hash. Changeable here by dropping or replacing the dep.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128-CMAC is used in sgx-api-lite to compute the MAC over an SGX report/quote body (Cmac::<Aes128> new_from_slice → update → finalize into_bytes), backing the sgx-api-lite dependency on cmac 0.7.1 — part of the local SGX attestation/report verification path. Changeable here. CMAC itself is symmetric and not Shor-relevant, but it depends on classical AES-128 and is graded below CNSA 2.0.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA (secp256k1 via sp_core) is the worker/signing signature scheme across this Phala confidential-computing monorepo: phactory recovers and verifies secp256k1 signatures on messages and EVM pubkeys (crates/phactory/api/src/crypto.rs), the pink chain-extension exposes sign/verify/public-key ops for SigType::Ecdsa, and the SDK/protobuf layer declares the Ecdsa SignatureType used in pruntime RPC. All 30 sites are live operations, protocol enum declarations, generated protobuf code, tests exercisi

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The project's ECDH is a custom Diffie-Hellman on the Ristretto255 group: phala-crypto's ecdh.rs builds keys from schnorrkel MiniSecretKey/SecretKey (expansion mode Ed25519) and agree() multiplies a curve25519-dalek Scalar by the schnorrkel PublicKey point — not X25519. The 32-byte shared secret is used directly as the AES key with no KDF ("Derives a secret key for symmetric encryption without a KDF", ecdh.rs:35). It backs the phactory secret channel and cluster-state files (ECDH agree → derive_k

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ed25519-dalek@2.0.0 is a direct declared dependency of the workspace (Cargo.lock), with Ed25519 JS libs declared in the e2e and scripts/js yarn.locks — the signature library behind the worker/identity signing surface also inventoried in the code-scan Ed25519 object. This is the dependency-inventory entry; presence is the question, and the build ships it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring@0.1.0 (workspace Cargo.lock) and the scripts/js X25519 JS package provide the X25519 agreement primitive — ring backs rustls's TLS key exchange for the phactory/prouter HTTPS sessions, and the JS side mirrors the worker ECDH protocol. Declared-dependency inventory entry; X25519 is harvest-now-decrypt-later exposed in any captured TLS session.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: curve25519-dalek 2.0 is the engine behind phala-crypto's ecdh module (the secret-channel key agreement confirmed in the ECDH object). The i2pd.rs site is the CryptoKeyTypeECIESX25519Aead constant — the I2P ECIES-X25519-AEAD suite the embedded router supports but generate_ident_to_file does not select (it picks ElGamal). X25519 key agreement is retroactively breakable by Shor.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: curve25519-dalek@2.1.3 is declared in Cargo.lock — the Curve25519 implementation backing phala-crypto's X25519 ECDH module (secret-channel key agreement) and Ed25519-adjacent key handling. Same asset as the phala-crypto/Cargo.toml entry confirmed under the X25519 object.

Records that classical P-256 ships in the build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-384 appears as the ECDSA-384-with-P-384 attestation key type in the SGX DCAP quote verification constants (sgx-attestation dcap) — Intel's attestation signature scheme, fixed by the vendor's quote format and DCAP collateral; observable here, replaceable only by Intel. The i2pd.rs sites are I2P signing-suite enum constants (ECDSA-P-384/P-521) supported by the embedded i2pd router but not selected by generate_ident_to_file (which picks Ed25519). Meets interim CNSA strength; still Shor-vulnerable

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-GCM is the AEAD protecting the phactory secret channel and encrypted message files: ring AES_256_GCM/AES_128_GCM unbound keys in phala-crypto, aes128gcm stream reader/writer for sealed files in phactory/prpc_service, and Node 'aes-256-gcm' in the frontend SDK and scripts/js pruntime client for the client side of the channel. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128-GCM is the stream cipher for the phactory secret channel and sealed message files (new_aes128gcm_writer/reader over ECDH-derived key128 in phactory and prpc_service), and AES-128 also backs the CMAC used by the SGX quote-mac layer in sgx-api-lite. ring AES_128_GCM and Aes128Gcm::from_key construct the live AEADs. Changeable here; below CNSA 2.0's 256-bit preference but quantum-resistant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (SHA-3 family) is used for EVM-style address derivation from secp256k1 public keys in phactory and the frontend SDK addressConverter, and as the trie hasher (KeccakHasher, keccak-hasher dep) for phala-trie-storage — the Ethereum-compatible Merkle-Patricia trie hashing. memdb.rs sites are the crate's own tests exercising the real hasher. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HKDF-SHA256 is the key-derivation function in phala-crypto: sr25519.rs derives worker subkeys (sr25519 key derivation) using hkdf::Salt::new(HKDF_SHA256, &KDF_SALT) with expand — KDF_SALT is a crate-level constant salt. HKDF on a classical secret; the derived keys inherit the input's quantum exposure. Changeable here.

SHA-256 is Grover-weakened but not broken; not urgent.
